title: Skin Disease (Tsara'at)
lead: The Hebrew tsara'at, traditionally "leprosy," names a group of scaly skin conditions, and mold in cloth and walls, that made a person or object ritually unclean (Leviticus 13–14). It is not Hansen's disease. Miriam, Naaman and Uzziah suffered it, and Jesus touched and healed those who had it.

sections.b: Moses' hand turns white "like snow" as a sign (Exodus 4:6). Miriam is struck after speaking against Moses and shut outside the camp seven days (Numbers 12:10–15). The Syrian general Naaman is healed by washing seven times in the Jordan, and Elisha's servant Gehazi takes on his disease through greed (2 Kings 5). Four men with skin disease at Samaria's gate find the Arameans' camp empty (2 Kings 7:3–10). King Uzziah is struck when he burns incense in the temple and lives in a separate house until he dies (2 Chronicles 26:19–21). In the Gospels Jesus touches and heals such people and sends them to the priests (Mark 1:40–45; Luke 17:11–19), and he sends the Twelve to "cleanse" them (Matthew 10:8).
